title: Graph Valid Tree
description:
You have a graph of `n` nodes labeled from `0` to `n - 1`. You are given an integer `n` and a list of `edges` where `edges[i] = [a_i, b_i]` indicates that there is an undirected edge between nodes `a_i` and `b_i` in the graph.

Return `true` if the edges of the given graph make up a **valid tree**, and `false` otherwise.

Recall that an undirected graph is a valid tree if and only if it is **fully connected** (there is a path between every pair of nodes) and **acyclic** (it contains no cycles).
constraints: There are no self-loops or repeated edges.
hints: A fundamental graph-theory characterization: an undirected graph on `n` vertices is a tree if and only if it has **exactly `n - 1` edges** AND is **fully connected** (equivalently, has `n - 1` edges and contains no cycle).
First check `edges.length == n - 1` — if not, you can immediately return `false` (fewer edges means disconnected; more edges guarantees a cycle).
With `edges.length == n - 1`, build an adjacency list and run BFS or DFS from node `0`, counting visited nodes. The graph is a valid tree if and only if all `n` nodes are visited.

examples.explanation: The 5 nodes are connected by 4 edges with no cycles, forming a valid tree.
Nodes 1, 2, and 3 form a cycle (1 - 2 - 3 - 1), so the graph is not a valid tree.
A single node with no edges is connected and acyclic, so it is a valid tree.
